chunks: Yūnus narrated from Yaḥyā al-Ḥalabī, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said:
A man asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger..."
He said: "That is up to the Imam; he carries out regarding him whatever he deems fit." I said: "So is that delegated entirely to him?" He said: "No, but according to the due measure of the crime."

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the divinely guided authority responsible for implementing the ruling
key_terms.الْجِنَايَةِ: the criminal offense whose degree determines the punishment
key_terms.يُحَارِبُونَ: they wage war or engage in hostile rebellion

ai.seo_question: Is the punishment for muḥārabah left entirely to the Imam’s discretion in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the application of the punishment mentioned in the verse concerning those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger is entrusted to the Imam. However, the Imam does not act arbitrarily; rather, the ruling is applied in accordance with the nature and extent of the offense committed.
